methods.notes: The app scans unfiltered and matches the advertised name exactly ("Multi_LED"), then parses manufacturer-specific data: byte 6 = firmware version, byte 7 = device type, byte 8 = paired flag (1 = bound). Whether the device also advertises the 0x1000 service UUID is unproven, so name matching is the documented mechanism.

device.name: ProGLOW Motorcycle LED Controller
device.notes:
Motorcycle ground-effect LED controller from com.ttcble.proglow static analysis (APK v4.7). Normal command sends are unencoded GATT writes to characteristic 0x1001. Packets start with header 0x3C; state/response parsing expects 0x4D — asynchronous 0x4D state packets arrive as notifications on 0x1002. No CRC/checksum was found in the normal command builder. FCC ID 2A55N-PG-BTBOX-1: STM32F103 MCU plus a Shengrun HY-40R201P BLE module (TI CC2541F256); Shengrun's public TTCBLEManager iOS SDK documents the same 0x1000/0x1001 GATT skeleton plus an optional `encryption:` write flag (unused here). The APK bundles an optional libhy_api.so traffic-obfuscation layer but the app disables it, so command/state traffic is plaintext. Firmware revision is read via DIS 0x2A26 (observed "V3.3"); no public firmware downloads exist.
Second protocol generation: the app's second-generation protocol package implements a parallel 0x3C-headed command set with motion()/motionColors() commands for newer hardware; the advertised manufacturer-data byte 7 device type selects which generation (and UI) the app drives. Latent OTA: the APK carries a full TI CC2541 OAD implementation (com/ble/ble/oad/) but with no call sites from app code and no firmware images — OTA is unused here.
Sibling product: the same app and protocol drive Custom Dynamics "Magical Wizards" 12V systems (per the app's Google Play listing).

credentials.notes: The password is generated by the app and kept in its private database; without it the device answers 4D 09 01 and the connection is dropped. Pairing is limited to one controller at a time.
stored_on_device: Per-device 6-byte BLE password (random, set at first pairing)
Paired/bound-phone state (advertised in mfr data byte 8)

factory_reset.effect: Clears the controller's pairing state (the per-device password and the bound-phone flag advertised in manufacturer data byte 8) so it can be paired to a new phone.

steps.action: Disconnect the blue battery-monitor wire from the battery.
Touch the blue battery-monitor wire on/off to the positive battery terminal 15 times.
steps.expect: LED accessories start flashing and color-cycling; the controller is ready to be paired to a new phone.

steps.action: Remove power (or battery) for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection.
steps.notes: Only drops the BLE link — the remedy for the 'already connected to another phone' failure mode, not a pairing reset.

methods.description: The device advertises as soon as it is powered on and accepts a BLE connection without OS-level pairing or a PIN, but lighting commands are gated behind the per-device six-byte password (0x09) command — a replacement client must know or recover that password, and the device pairs to only one controller at a time (see factory_reset for moving it to a new phone).

steps.action: Power the device and scan for its advertisement.
Connect and run the documented initialization sequence, if the spec defines one.

setup.notes: No network provisioning, but the controller expects a six-byte password command before it accepts lighting commands. The password is a RANDOM 6-byte per-device secret the app generates at first pairing (Data.randomPassword(6)) and stores in its private DeviceDB — not a shared default. A wrong password gets a 4D 09 01 reply and the app disconnects ("password error"). The vendor limits pairing to one device at a time.

rejoin.notes: The device holds pairing state: the per-device random password acts as a binding secret, advertisement manufacturer-data byte 8 carries a paired flag (and the app tracks isBindOther), and the vendor documents the blue-wire 15-touch reset as MANDATORY to pair a new phone. Power-cycling alone only drops the current link.

power_off.description: All channels OFF (set_power with channel_mask=0x0F, on_off=0).

power_on.description: All channels ON (set_power with channel_mask=0x0F, on_off=1).

set_home_multi_color.description: Set home/multi-color mode; 20-byte packet with up to four RGB triples in first packet

packet_layout.7: RGB triples, up to four colors in first packet; additional colors use second 20-byte packet

channel_mask.description: Bit mask of the channels this packet addresses. Same set as set_power minus 0x0F, which the vendor app does not send on this command.

set_power.description: Set on/off for a channel mask

channel_mask.description: Bit mask of the channels this command addresses. A set rather than a range: only these combinations appear in the vendor app, so a client offers a choice instead of a 0-15 slider.

set_speed.description: Set effect speed; app sends 6 - speed

sync_time.description: Sync device time and protection settings (12 bytes in the current app; 2023 V3.3-era on-wire captures show a 14-byte frame with 3 extra trailing bytes)

characteristics.name: Command Write
characteristics.notes: All observed ProGLOW commands target this characteristic and start with 0x3C.

characteristics.name: State Notify
characteristics.notes: Asynchronous 0x4D state packets arrive as notifications here: BleService.enableNotification targets CHARACTERS[1] (=0x1002) and the on-wire capture shows the CCC write 0x1002/0x2902 = [01 00] followed by streaming 0x4D… packets.

characteristics.name: Read
characteristics.notes: Register-read response channel only (readReg writes a register index to 0x1005, then reads 0x1004); not the async state channel.
